text:
I need to send a quarterly update to our investors. I'm the founder of a scheduling app for physical therapy clinics. We have 6 people.

Numbers for the quarter:
- Monthly recurring revenue is $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- We added 9 clinics and lost 4. One of the 4 was our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain that paid $5,500 a month. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system.
- We have $480,000 in the bank and lose about $44,000 a month.
- Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, against 13% before they started.
- I didn't send updates for the last two quarters.
- Next month we start selling the reminder feature on its own for $150 a month.

Under 500 words. It goes to 11 investors.

Before I draft this I need a few answers from you. The update has to do three things for these 11 readers. It should own the two missed updates, explain why revenue stayed flat, and show that the reminder product is a real answer to what you lost. Your numbers already support part of that:

- **Without the chain, revenue grew about 15% this quarter.** Losing them cost $5,500 a month, yet monthly revenue stayed at $41,000. So the rest of the business went from about $35,500 to $41,000 a month.
- **You have about 11 months of cash left** ($480k ÷ $44k a month). That puts the end around October 2027. Investors will work this out within seconds, so the update should do it first.
- **The open risk is the chain's reason for leaving.** Schedulers built into electronic records systems could pull away other customers too. Selling reminders on their own may be your answer to that, if they work alongside those built-in schedulers.

**Questions, most important first:**

1. **What's the plan for the 11 months?** Are you raising, cutting costs, or aiming to break even? Is there a specific ask for these investors, like introductions, a bridge round or advice? This decides how the update ends.
2. **Do standalone reminders work for clinics using their records system's built-in scheduler?** If yes, the chain's departure becomes the case for the new product. Also, do you have any early signs of demand, such as a waitlist, pilot clinics or prices you've tested? And is there a target you'll commit to, like "X reminder customers by [date]"?
3. **How many of your current clinics use records systems with a built-in scheduler?** Investors will ask how exposed you are to losing more customers this way.
4. **Why did the last two updates not go out, and what cadence will you commit to now?** One honest sentence near the top works better than skipping over it.
5. **How solid is the 7% vs 13% no-show figure?** How many clinics and what time period is it based on? This decides whether I state it plainly or add a caveat.
6. **Housekeeping and anything I'm missing:**
   - Your name for the sign-off, and how you greet these investors.
   - Is the chain one of the 4 clinics lost, or 12 of them?
   - Any team changes or other news.
   - Anything investors will learn later that's better said now?

Once you answer, I'll write the full update, under 500 words.

1. I don't have a raise or cut plan to share yet. What I want from investors is 20 minutes on the phone each, and intros to clinic chains.

2. I don't know for sure whether they work alongside the built-in schedulers. On demand, 6 clinics have said they'll buy reminders on their own when it launches December 1. I don't have a target to commit to.

3. Two other customers use the same records system as the chain that left. Together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way.

4. I skipped them because the numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. No other reason. From now on I'll send an update in the first week of every quarter, and the next one goes out January 7. I'll also send a monthly one-page set of numbers to any investor who asks.

5. I don't know the clinic count or time period behind it offhand.

6. I'm Sam Patel, and the company is Cadence Scheduling. I don't have a set greeting, so use whatever you think fits. The chain counted as one of the 4 lost. No team changes. The only other thing is what I said in 3: I can't promise the customers on that records system will stay.

I wrote the update from your answers. It's about 440 words.

<final_document>
Subject: Cadence Scheduling: quarterly update, and an apology for the gap

Hi all,

I'll start with an apology. I didn't send updates for the last two quarters. The numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. That was the wrong call, because bad news is exactly what you should hear from me early. From now on you'll get an update in the first week of every quarter. The next one goes out January 7. If you'd like a one-page set of numbers every month as well, reply and I'll send it.

**The quarter in numbers**

- Monthly recurring revenue: $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- Clinics: 9 added, 4 lost.
- Cash: $480,000 in the bank. We lose about $44,000 a month, which gives us roughly 11 months, to around October 2027, if nothing changes.

**What happened**

Our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain paying $5,500 a month, moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system. Revenue held flat only because the rest of the business grew. Without that chain, monthly revenue went from about $35,500 to $41,000, roughly 15% in one quarter.

There's a risk I want you to see clearly. Two other customers use the same records system as the chain that left, and together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way. If they do, monthly revenue falls to $37,200.

**What's working**

Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, against 13% before they started. It's the clearest result we deliver.

**What's next**

On December 1 we start selling reminders on their own for $150 a month. Six clinics have already said they'll buy at launch. I don't yet know whether the reminders will work alongside the schedulers built into records systems. That's the question I most want answered. If they do, a clinic that moves its scheduling to its records system could still stay with us for reminders. I'm not setting a sales target yet. You'll see the real numbers on January 7.

I don't have a fundraising or cost-cutting plan to share yet. With about 11 months of cash, I need to settle that soon. I'd rather work it out with your input than hand you a finished plan.

**What I'm asking for**

1. **20 minutes on the phone with each of you.** Reply with a few times that work and I'll set it up.
2. **Introductions to physical therapy clinic chains.** A chain is the single biggest customer we lost, and it's where one deal moves our numbers most.

Thank you for your patience over the last six months. I'll keep you better informed from here.

Sam Patel
Founder, Cadence Scheduling
</final_document>

A few things to check before you send:

- **No-show figure:** I gave it without saying how many clinics or what time period it covers, because you didn't have that to hand. If any of these investors is likely to ask, find the sample size before your calls.
- **The 15% growth:** I worked this out from your numbers rather than you giving it to me: $41,000 minus the chain's $5,500 is $35,500 three months ago. Check it against your books before it goes out.
- **The $37,200 figure:** This is what monthly revenue would be if both customers on that records system left. It's there to show you've measured the risk, not to predict that they will.
- **The ending:** It deliberately says you don't have a plan for when the cash runs out yet. That's true, and it turns the 20-minute calls into a request for advice rather than a formality.
